title: The first humans: Tautavel, Chauvet and Lascaux
story: Imagine a cave in the Pyrenees foothills, around 450,000 years ago. A small group of hunters gathers round a fire. They have stone tools, no writing and no name for the land. We call that land "France" only today: it is where our long road really starts, long before the signposts of L1.
objective: I can name three key sites of prehistory in France and say what each one teaches us.

write.heading: 1. Prehistory
write.body: **Prehistory** is the time before writing. In France it covers hundreds of thousands of years, so it is much longer than all the periods of L1 together (→ L1). We know it only from bones, tools and paintings.

write.heading: 2. Three key sites
write.body:
| Site | Date | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Tautavel** (Pyrenees) | around **450,000 years ago** | one of the oldest humans of Europe; hunters with fire and stone tools |
| **Chauvet** (Ardèche) | around **36,000 years ago** | among the oldest cave paintings in the world |
| **Lascaux** (Dordogne) | around **17,000 years ago** | huge painted bulls and horses; found in **1940** |

write.heading: 3. Two kinds of humans
write.body: **Neanderthals** lived in Europe for a long time. **Homo sapiens**, our own species, arrived around **45,000 years ago**. The two met, and then the Neanderthals disappeared, around 40,000 years ago. Historians still debate why.

write.heading: 4. Draw
write.body: A map of France with three dots: Tautavel, Chauvet and Lascaux, and a horse or a bull from Lascaux.

check.a: The time before writing, known only from bones, tools and paintings.

check.q: Match each site with its date: Tautavel, Chauvet, Lascaux.
check.a: Tautavel around 450,000 years ago; Chauvet around 36,000; Lascaux around 17,000 (found in 1940).

check.q: Which human species are we, and when did it arrive in Europe?

read_more: Lascaux was found on 12 September 1940 by four teenagers and a dog. The cave was closed to visitors in 1963 because breath was damaging the paintings. Today you can visit a full copy nearby. The Chauvet cave, found in 1994, is also closed; its copy is in the Ardèche. Chauvet is a UNESCO World Heritage site (2014).
next: Next lesson: about 6,000 years ago, people stop hunting only and start farming. They also raise the stones of Carnac.
